title: Semantic Entropy Probes: Robust and Cheap Hallucination Detection
one_line_claim: Semantic entropy probes predict hallucinations from hidden states at single token positions without multi-sample computation.
method_summary: Train linear logistic regression classifiers on hidden states from token-before-generation (TBG) or second-last token (SLT) position to predict semantic entropy. Semantic entropy is computed by sampling N=10 generations, clustering by semantic equivalence via NLI, and computing Shannon entropy over clusters. SEPs eliminate need for multiple samples at test time by approximating semantic entropy from a single generation's hidden representation.

key_findings.finding: SEPs achieve strong AUROC for hallucination detection while eliminating the 5-10x computational cost of multi-sample semantic entropy.
key_findings.quote: reduces the overhead of semantic uncertainty quantification to almost zero...had a 5-to-10-fold increase in computation cost.

key_findings.finding: SEPs generalize better than accuracy probes out-of-distribution: +7.7 to +10.5 AUROC points across leave-one-dataset-out evaluation.
key_findings.quote: SEPs outperform accuracy probes significantly: +7.7 to +10.5 AUROC points. Mistral-7B: 10.5+/-3.5 point advantage. Llama-2-7B: 7.7+/-1.3 point advantage

key_findings.finding: Hidden states encode semantic uncertainty before generation begins; SEPs trained on TBG enable single-pass detection.
key_findings.quote: SEPs can capture semantic entropy even before generation...enabling single-pass uncertainty quantification

relation_to_herald.shared: Both use learned classifiers on per-token model states to detect quality degradation during or before generation. Both operate at inference time with minimal overhead.
differs_on: HERALD predicts compression-induced catastrophic failures (looping, non-termination) under KV-cache compression; SEPs detect general hallucinations in standard inference with no compression context.
HERALD trains XGBoost on per-token logit probabilities/entropy; SEPs train linear probes on hidden states at fixed positions, not on logit signals.
HERALD predicts failure onset H tokens ahead for pre-onset intervention; SEPs classify whether output is semantically uncertain post-hoc.
